title: We love because (1 John 4:19–21)
hookLine: we love him because he first loved us

cards: Stand at the edge of a canyon and say nothing, and the canyon says nothing back. Call out, and a moment later the rock answers in your own voice. An echo never goes first.
It only exists because something reached it. Today the writer of First John asks where love comes from in the first place.
The passage is three verses long, and its first line is about exactly that: which love comes first, and which one answers.

teach.b: In the King James Bible: "We love him, because he first loved us." Short enough to carry, and some readers hear the whole letter in it.
In the writer's telling, our love is a response, and God's love goes first. Some readers also notice that the line still stands without the word him: we love, because he first loved us.
Read that way, it's not only that we love God because God loved us. We love at all, anyone at all, because we were loved first.

Then the writer makes it concrete, and uncomfortable: "If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?"
He's not being harsh for fun. God is invisible.
Your brother is right in front of you, irritating habits and all. If you can't love the one you can see, the claim to love the one you can't is hard to believe.
It's a test anyone can turn on themselves, and the letter doesn't pretend anyone passes it cleanly.
Maybe that's why it comes right after the line about who loved first. Then: "And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also."

One commandment, pointing two ways: up toward the God no one has seen, and sideways toward the brother in the next chair. The letter has circled this from its first page, light, children, deeds, fear, and here it lands.

how: 1 John 4:19 is a short verse some Christians memorize as a summary of their faith, and some churches teach it to children.

o: a love that answers, because it was loved first
a love that fades the farther it travels
a promise repeated until it's believed

games.q: what's inside 1 John 4:19–21 — tap the pairs.
p: who says I love God, and hates his brother
the test of loving the God unseen
who loves God loves his brother also

s: the writer says our love comes first, and God answers it
the other way round: we love him, because he first loved us.
the writer calls someone who says he loves God but hates his brother a liar
the writer treats loving your brother as optional for someone who loves God
it's a commandment: he who loves God loves his brother also.

games.q: someone says, I love God, but I can't stand my brother. what does the letter ask?
o: how can he love God whom he hath not seen?
is his brother really so bad?
games.why: "he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?"

practice: For a minute, don't try to love anyone; remember being loved instead, a parent's voice, a friend who stayed, a stranger's kindness on a bad day, and stay in that one memory without hurrying to pay it back.
If you pray, receive God's love the same way, with nothing to do but be loved. Only at the end, notice whether anything in you wants to answer.

wordCard.voice: Echo. The hook's picture for our love: it never goes first, First John says, because he first loved us, and we only answer back.
